(i) the levels of MCP and CR1 transcripts are significantly higher in SLE patients compared to normal controls, (ii) the levels of CR1 and MCP mRNA transcripts are significantly higher and DAF mRNA transcript is significantly lower in active SLE patients compared with inactive SLE patients, (iii) CR1 and MCP levels in active SLE are significantly lower in patients with good response to immunosuppressive drugs compared with those with poor response to the drugs, (iv) MCP and CR
the level of MCP and CR1 transcripts in peripheral blood leukocytes and plasma are significantly higher in patients with active SLE than those with inactive disease.
the levels of membrane bound CRPs DAF, MCP and CD59 are decreased in SLE, while CR1 levels are increased in SLE, and the levels of DAF, CR1, MCP, and CD59 are correlated with SLE disease activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and validation of novel disease activity biomarkers and therapeutic strategies for the management of SLE.
the development of noninvasive biomarker(s) for SLE disease and response to treatment and identification of potential therapeutic target(s).
the identification of novel noninvasive biomarker for the diagnosis and prognosis of SLE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
membrane bound CRPs are not only biomarkers but also therapeutic targets for S.LE.
the level of Daf, Mcp, and Cr1 transcripts in peripheral blood leukocytes and CD59 in serum could be used as biomarkers for SLS disease activity.
the level of DAP, MCP, CRl, and CD59 in SLE patients is significantly different from healthy individuals, and these proteins are potential noninvasive disease markers for SLE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of membrane bound complement regulatory protein transcripts in PBMCs of patients with SLE is a reliable marker of SLE disease activity.
the levels of MCP, DAF, CR1, CD59 transcripts, and proteins are significantly altered in SLE and these alterations correlate with the disease activity.
the level of DDAF, MCP, CRl, and CD59 mRNA transcripts in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) may be used as noninvasive biomarker for disease activity in SIE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
membrane bound complement regulators are potential biomarkers and therapeutic target proteins for SLE.
these proteins can be used as noninvasive biomarker for disease activity and as therapeutic target for SLE.
membrane bound complement inhibitors may be used as noninvasive biomarker for SLE.
